questions.question: What is the value of the 6 in 136 482 and the 6 in 765 430, and why are they different?
questions.expected_answer: In 136 482 the 6 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 6 000. In 765 430 the 6 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 60 000. The ten thousands place is worth ten times the thousands place.

questions.question: Write 300 000 plus 4 000 plus 50 plus 9 as one number and explain where the zeros come from.
questions.expected_answer: 304 059. There are no ten thousands and no hundreds, so zeros hold those two places and keep the 3, 4, 5 and 9 in their correct seats.

questions.question: Use the cards 4, 0, 7, 2, 9 and 5 to make the biggest and the smallest six-digit numbers, and explain your choices.
questions.expected_answer: Biggest: 975 420, because the biggest digits go in the places worth the most. Smallest: 204 579. The smallest digits go on the left, but 0 cannot be first or the number would only have five digits, so 2 goes first and 0 goes second.
